item.title: Peace – the new product placement
item.description: Protestors of the Trump administration are strategically increasing their market share of public opinion by offering a better product: peace.

item.title: CT trooper’s deliberate crash launches legal, political complications
item.description: Last year, a CT state trooper stopped a speeding car with a 'pit maneuver.' No one was injured, but an investigation is underway.

item.title: As reports of online exploitation grow, CT leaders try new strategies
item.description: CT officials are considering new regulations on social media and gaming companies to protect youths, but advocates say there's more to do.

item.title: Hartford looks to end parking contract with ICE
item.description: In a letter, Hartford Mayor Arunan Arulampalam asked HPA to terminate an agreement allowing ICE employees to use a city-owned parking lot.

item.title: Murphy objects to Homeland Security funding over lack of reforms
item.description: Republicans sought short-term DHS funding to continue talks, but Sen. Chris Murphy objected on behalf of the Democrats. A shutdown is likely.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries stumps in district safe for Dems, if not for Larson
item.description: Hakeem Jeffries' efforts on behalf of Larson were personal, not political. CT's 1st District is competitive only in a Democratic primary.

item.title: In CT, educational opportunity is still decided by ZIP code
item.description: Connecticut must reduce its reliance on local property taxes and fully modernize the Education Cost Sharing formula.

item.title: CT’s financial emergency is over. The funding is not
item.description: The newly adopted S.B. 83 does more than preserve unused balances. It entrenches the fund and expands its scope.
